title: Packet Capture Configuration
description: Capture packets from one or more network interfaces, or decode a pcap file. Live capture is supported on Linux (AF_PACKET) and macOS (/dev/bpf) and needs elevated privileges - run the 'Check permissions' action first. Decoding a pcap needs no privileges at all.

interfaces.title: Interfaces
interfaces.description: Interfaces to capture from, in parallel. Each one becomes its own trace source. Leave empty when using Replay PCAP File.

interface.title: Interface
interface.description: Network interface to capture on (eth0, en0, wlan0, lo, ...). Pick a device from the list, or type a name - the list comes from the machine running the agent and appears once the extension has run there at least once.

name.title: Name
name.description: Trace source name for this interface; catalog paths read <name>.pkt.<field>. Defaults to the interface name. Dots, colons and '@' are replaced with '_' because they are catalog path separators.

snaplen.title: Snapshot Length (bytes)
snaplen.description: Bytes captured per packet; the rest is truncated. 512 keeps the whole embedded/industrial control plane byte-complete - every legal Modbus-TCP frame (MBAP 7 + PDU up to 253, about 314 B once Ethernet/IP/TCP headers are counted), DHCP (whose semantics live in the options after the 236-byte BOOTP area), DNS and mDNS responses, MQTT CONNECT, DoIP, SOME/IP and PTP - while cutting bulk transfers so a file copy does not fill the trace. 128 would break DHCP and DNS responses outright. Raise it only when you need full payloads.

promiscuous.title: Promiscuous Mode
promiscuous.description: Capture every frame on the segment, not just frames addressed to this host. Off by default: on a switched network it mostly adds noise, it can require extra privileges, and some drivers and VM NICs lose throughput sharply in promiscuous mode. Turn it on when capturing from a mirror/SPAN port or a tap.

buffer_size.title: Kernel Buffer Size (bytes)
buffer_size.description: Kernel capture buffer for this interface. Larger buffers absorb bursts without kernel drops, at the cost of RAM. If the 'dropped' counter in the 'Capture stats' action climbs, raise this.

exclude_agent_traffic.title: Exclude Agent Traffic
exclude_agent_traffic.description: Drop packets to and from the Zelos agent's own address and port. Leave this on. The extension publishes every captured packet to the agent over the network, so capturing that traffic feeds the extension its own output: a captured packet emits a row, the row is sent to the agent, and that send is itself captured. At large snapshot lengths a row is larger than the packet that produced it, so the loop amplifies instead of settling - it is divergent, not merely noisy. Turn it off only when capturing an interface that carries no agent traffic.

replay_pcap.title: Replay PCAP File
replay_pcap.description: Decode a .pcap/.pcapng file instead of capturing live. This path opens no capture handle and needs no privileges, so it works on any machine - use it to try the extension, or to analyze a capture someone sent you. When set, the Interfaces list is ignored and the extension exits once the file is decoded.

log_frames.title: Log Raw Frames
log_frames.description: Populate the 'frame' Binary column with the captured bytes (up to the frame storage limit). Turn it off to keep only decoded header fields, which makes traces far smaller.

frame_snaplen.title: Frame Storage Limit (bytes)
frame_snaplen.description: Bytes of each packet stored in the 'frame' column. Storage only: dissection always reads every captured byte, so the decoded columns are the same whatever this is set to, and 'orig_len'/'cap_len'/'truncated' keep describing capture truncation rather than this limit. null (the default) stores every captured byte, so the snapshot length is the single byte budget and the control plane stays byte-complete in the frame column - Modbus-TCP, DHCP, DNS/mDNS. Set a number to store only a prefix and shrink traces.
